subtitle: When a kingdom of learning tasted the weight of its own crown

panels.action: Jayapida Vinayaditya stands in a Kashmiri palace courtyard between two groups—robed scholars on one side, stern tax officials on the other—with snow peaks behind and storm clouds gathering above.

dialogue.text: In Jayapida Vinayaditya’s Kashmir, the same king who built a court of learning would strain it with his taxes—leaving history to weigh patron and tyrant in one man.

i18n.hi: जयपीड विनयादित्य के कश्मीर में वही राजा जिसने विद्वानों का दरबार खड़ा किया, उसी पर करों का बोझ डालता है — इतिहास को एक ही आदमी में संरक्षक और जालिम तौलने देता हुआ।

panels.shot: slow push-in from palace terrace to valley
panels.action: Jayapida stands on a high terrace of the Karkota capital, looking over the lush Kashmir valley dotted with temple spires and quiet monasteries under a pale morning light.

dialogue.text: By the late eighth century, the Karkota kings of Kashmir ruled a valley thick with temples, land grants and learning—wealth measured not only in gold, but in words.

i18n.hi: आठवीं सदी के अंत तक, कर्कोटा राजाओं का कश्मीर घाटी में मंदिरों, भू-दान और विद्या से लदा था — जहाँ दौलत सोने से ही नहीं, शब्दों से भी नापी जाती थी।

panels.action: Inside a pillared audience hall, Jayapida sits on a modest throne, leaning forward with alert eyes as Brahmin scholars read from palm-leaf manuscripts before him.

dialogue.text: Kalhana later remembered Jayapida as a king who gathered Brahmin scholars from many lands, bending a warrior’s ear toward poetry, law and story.

i18n.hi: कल्हण ने जयपीड को उस राजा की तरह याद किया जो दूर-दूर से ब्राह्मण विद्वान जुटाता था, योद्धा के कान कविता, नीति और कथा की ओर मोड़ता था।

panels.shot: wide shot of diverse scholars before the throne
panels.action: A wide view of the royal court shows rows of scholars with varied dress—some in Northwestern styles, others in Southern, some visibly foreign to the valley—seated on low mats before Jayapida.

dialogue.text: From the Indus lands to distant Dravida, migrant Brahmins and literati found their way to Jayapida’s court, turning Kashmir into a crossroads of learning.

i18n.hi: इंद्र की धरती से दूर द्रविड तक, प्रवासी ब्राह्मण और साहित्यकार जयपीड के दरबार तक आए, कश्मीर को विद्या का संगम बना दिया।

panels.action: In a quieter chamber, Jayapida examines copper-plate land grant records spread on a low table, priests and ministers gesturing to maps of fields and villages.

dialogue.text: These scholars did not live by praise alone. They were fed by agraharas—tax-free village grants to Brahmins and temples, woven into the kingdom’s revenue.

i18n.hi: ये विद्वान सिर्फ प्रशंसा से नहीं जीते थे। उन्हें आहार मिलता था अग्रहारों से — ब्राह्मणों और मंदिरों को मिली कर-मुक्त बस्तियाँ, जो राज्य की आमदनी में गुँथी थीं।

panels.shot: close-up on Jayapida’s face, half in light, half in shadow
panels.action: Jayapida’s thoughtful face fills the frame, one side lit by the glow of an oil lamp over manuscripts, the other shaded, as if weighed by unseen calculations.

dialogue.text: Kalhana praises Jayapida’s gatherings of wise men, yet in the same breath warns that this king would later turn his hand against the very grants that sustained them.

i18n.hi: कल्हण बुद्धिमानों की जयपीड-सभा की तारीफ करता है, पर साथ ही चेतावनी भी देता है कि यही राजा बाद में उन दान पर ही हाथ उलटा रखता है जो उन्हें सँभाले हुए थे।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye over court and treasury officials
panels.action: From above, the court shows a contrast: one side a learned assembly with scrolls, the other a cluster of royal treasurers and tax collectors around chests and account boards.

dialogue.text: No royal record survives to explain his choice. We see only hints—a king balancing generosity with the hard arithmetic of war, building projects and a straining treasury.

i18n.hi: कोई शाही दस्तावेज उसकी चाल साफ नहीं करता। हमें बस इशारे दिखते हैं — एक राजा जो उदारता को जंग, निर्माण और कराहती कोष की सख्त गिनती से तौल रहा है।

panels.action: Jayapida sits rigid in the audience hall as a royal scribe reads from a decree; in the background, Brahmins exchange anxious glances, clutching their document bundles.

dialogue.text: Kalhana’s chronicle tells of a turn: Jayapida, once patron, is said to have rescinded or burdened agraharas, drawing scholars’ lands back into the tax net.

i18n.hi: कल्हण की कहानी मोड़ सुनाती है: जयपीड, जो कभी संरक्षक था, कहा जाता है कि उसने अग्रहारें वापस लीं या उन पर बोझ डाला, विद्वानों की जमीन को फिर कर-खाते में खींच लिया।

panels.shot: medium shot of a single Brahmin before the throne
panels.action: A senior Brahmin stands before Jayapida, hands respectfully folded, his expression a mix of hurt and restraint, while the king listens with a closed, unreadable face.

dialogue.speaker: jayapida_vinayaditya
dialogue.text: If the kingdom starves, what use are empty honors to anyone?

i18n.hi: अगर राज्य ही भूख से तड़पे, तो खाली सम्मान का किसी को क्या फ़ायदा?

panels.action: Rows of Brahmins and their families quietly leave a Kashmiri settlement at dawn, carrying bundles of manuscripts and household goods, while the distant palace sits still against the hills.

dialogue.text: In Kalhana’s telling, Brahmins felt betrayed. Harsh collections drove many away from their homes, thinning the very learned presence the king had fostered.

i18n.hi: कल्हण के शब्दों में, ब्राह्मण खुद को ठगा हुआ महसूस करते हैं। कड़की वसूली ने कई लोगों को घर छोड़ने पर मजबूर किया, वही विद्वत उपस्थिति पतली कर दी जो राजा ने खुद पाली थी।

panels.action: Jayapida walks through a palace courtyard once crowded with teachers and students; now only a few scholars remain, and mosaic floors lie mostly empty under cold light.

dialogue.text: Kalhana writes with the hurt of a Brahmin observer, his verses turning fiscal decrees into a moral lesson: when a king taxes trust, the court itself grows hollow.

i18n.hi: कल्हण ब्राह्मण दर्शक की चोट से लिखता है, उसके श्लोक राजकीय कर-फरमान को नैतिक पाठ बना देते हैं: जब राजा भरोसे पर कर लगाता है, दरबार के भीतर ही खालीपन घुस जाता है।

panels.shot: close-up on manuscript and royal seal
panels.action: A hand places a royal seal on a tax order, while above, a half-unrolled manuscript shows a poetic verse praising Jayapida’s generosity, the two texts visually at odds.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars place these events in a wider pattern—a possible revenue crisis, military campaigns and numismatic signs of strain behind Kalhana’s stories of tyranny.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक इतिहासकार इन घटनाओं को बड़े परिप्रेक्ष्य में रखते हैं — शायद आमदनी का संकट, सैन्य मुहिमें और सिक्कों के तनाव के संकेत, जिनके पीछे कल्हण की ज़ुल्म की कहानियाँ चलती हैं।

panels.action: Jayapida sits with ministers and learned advisers in a circle, some in courtly dress, others with Brahmin marks, debating over palm-leaf records and coin heaps.

dialogue.text: Somendra later notes that Narendra, ancestor of the poet Kshemendra, served as Jayapida’s minister—evidence that politics and letters still met in his inner circle.

i18n.hi: सोमेंद्र आगे लिखता है कि नरेंद्र, कवि क्षेमेंद्र का पुरखा, जयपीड का मंत्री था — सबूत कि सियासत और साहित्य अभी भी उसके अंतरंग घेरों में साथ बैठते थे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Jayapida in semi-dark audience hall
panels.action: Jayapida sits alone in the dim durbar, the throne elevated yet bare around him, as distant temple bells ring and snowlight filters in from far windows.

dialogue.text: The king who opened his doors to scholars from distant coasts now seemed, in Brahmin memory, to have shut those doors with demands for revenue.

i18n.hi: जो राजा दूर दरिया-किनारों से आए विद्वानों के लिए दरवाज़े खोलता था, वही अब ब्राह्मणों की याद में उन दरवाज़ों को महसूली मांगों से बंद करता हुआ दिखता है।

panels.action: The Kashmir valley at dusk shows villages, fields and shrines; smoke curls from homes, while temple silhouettes stand quiet against the fading sky.

dialogue.text: We cannot see the whole ledger—only the valley that lived between two courts: the court of learned men, and the court of royal collectors, both shaping Jayapida’s reign.

i18n.hi: हम पूरी हुकूमती हिसाब किताब नहीं देख पाते — बस वो घाटी जो दो दरबारों के बीच जीती थी: विद्वानों का दरबार, और शाही वसूलदारों का दरबार, दोनों मिलकर जयपीड का राज गढ़ते हुए।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on a later scribe’s hand
panels.action: Centuries later, a Kashmiri scribe copies Kalhana’s Rajatarangini on fresh palm leaves, the stylus carving Jayapida’s name into the record beside verses of praise and reproach.

dialogue.text: Kalhana’s Rajatarangini preserves Jayapida’s image in double lines—patron of scholarship, burden on Brahmin lands—reminding us that memory itself is shaped by those who write.

i18n.hi: कल्हण की राजतरंगिणी जयपीड की छवि दोहरी पंक्तियों में बचाती है — विद्या का संरक्षक, ब्राह्मण भूमियों पर बोझ — याद दिलाती है कि स्मृति खुद उन हाथों से बनती है जो लिखते हैं।

panels.action: In a symbolic scene, Jayapida stands before two empty seats in his court—one for a scholar, one for a tax officer—as the snow peaks glow with first light beyond the palace.

dialogue.text: Jayapida’s double court asks a question that survives him: when a ruler draws too hard on the lands that nourish thought, how many future voices are quietly taxed away?

i18n.hi: जयपीड का दोहरा दरबार एक सवाल छोड़ जाता है: जब शासक सोच को पालने वाली जमीनों को ज़्यादा निचोड़ता है, तो कितनी आने वाली आवाज़ें चुपचाप कर में कट जाती हैं?

subtitle_i18n.en: When a kingdom of learning tasted the weight of its own crown
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब ज्ञान का राज्य अपनी ही ताज की ठोकर चखता है
